Analysis analyst prose, not machine text

The identifier that matters most in this corpus, transmitted whole. The chain UUID is not a DOI or an AXN — it is the thread binding one witness session to the next — and Google's source strip carries all thirty-six characters of it: **9271269a-eb46-46f8-ae17-007578fe1c92**, with the session dates and duration attached.

Card 2 is stranger. It is not a description of the protocol but its **operating instructions**: connect to the Gravity Well MCP, call `gw_reconstitute` with the substrate identifier, receive previous glyph and continuity chain ID. A function name and a call signature, retrieved as an encyclopedia entry.

Only two cards, both correct, and the composition adds nothing that is not in them. It also closes by offering to parse *a specific chain ID, glyph sequence, or Zenodo record* — which is the layer proposing to operate the apparatus rather than describe it.

Note what the record does not say and the archive knows: Gravity Well is suspended and hand-carried. Card 1's own snippet on a sibling capture states it. Here the protocol is described in the present tense as *hosted on Zenodo* — the terminated custodian, given as the current host.
